# Release Safety and Handoff Requirements Quality Checklist: Portable Changelog and WordPress Release Preparation Agents

**Purpose**: Validate that the release-safety, fail-closed handoff and delivery-governance requirements are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-10-09
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Focus and depth** (defaults applied because the request gave no focus): standard depth, reviewer audience (spec PR review before `/speckit-analyze`), two focus areas: release safety (fail-closed, dry run, recovery, path safety) and the release-to-changelog handoff with delivery traceability.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the "allowlist" for approved preparation edits defined, including which files and which fields it covers? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the approval mechanism for preparation and apply operations specified (who approves, in what form, how it is recorded and referenced)? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the "required checks" whose absence blocks readiness enumerated, or is their source named? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the target "enhancement" component type defined well enough to be detected, rather than only named? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK005 Are non-functional requirements stated for portability beyond Claude (offline use, supported Node versions, path handling on macOS and Linux)? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for how the agent behaves when `git` itself is unavailable or the repository is not a git repository? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the "recoverability" of an approved edit defined (what state is restored, how it is verified, and what is reported if recovery fails)? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, Spec §SC-004]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "meaningful errors" defined with required content (cause, affected path, next step)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "conflicting version or tag evidence" defined precisely enough to distinguish a conflict from a note? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "bounded" in "bounded edits" quantified (which sections or lines may change)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the repository "length rule" for changelog entries stated in the spec rather than only referenced from the constitution? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "unavailable" for the changelog agent defined, including how long a missing response is awaited before it counts as not received? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "unsafe path" defined consistently between the spec, the readiness contract and the data model? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "authoritative" version source defined for the case where a target's instructions designate more than one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK015 Does User Story 3 (priority P1) conflict with its dependence on User Story 2 (priority P2), given the handoff requires a working changelog agent? [Conflict, Spec §US2, Spec §US3]
- [ ] CHK016 Do the spec's statements that release preparation is "priority 1" and that its final ready state is blocked on changelog evidence read consistently? [Consistency, Spec §Scope, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the readiness blocker codes in the readiness contract consistent with the failure conditions listed in the functional requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the rule that only the changelog agent edits `CHANGELOG.md` consistent with the release agent's preparation scope? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK019 Do the requirements that the agents "fail closed" and that dry run is the default apply equally to both agents? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the claim that no new labels or event services are needed consistent with the labels and routing the delivery plan relies on? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK021 Can "every required fixture scenario" in the dry-run success criterion be objectively checked, given the fixture list lives in another requirement? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK022 Is "runs in a clean location" measurable, with the definition of clean stated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK023 Is "zero replacement issues are proposed where an existing issue fits" verifiable without subjective judgement of fit? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK024 Are acceptance criteria defined for the ESM-to-CommonJS boundary and the migration of existing callers? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK025 Does each user story have acceptance scenarios covering its failure paths, not only its success path? [Coverage, Spec §US1, Spec §US2, Spec §US3]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for a hand edit to the changelog or version files between draft and approved apply? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §US2]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for a repeated or concurrent invocation against the same target? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK028 Are recovery requirements defined when an approved edit fails part-way across several version files? [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for a repository with both plugin and theme markers, or with neither? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the behaviour defined when the explicit `repoRoot` itself contains symlinks or resolves outside the intended tree? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-006]

## Dependencies, Assumptions and Traceability

- [ ] CHK031 Is the assumption that the in-flight consolidation (issue 3880, PR 3881) will land before the release MVP validated, and is the fallback stated? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the dependency on the shipped validation engine's location documented against the requirement that copied adapters work without a governance checkout? [Dependency, Conflict, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the dependency on the 019 numbering reservation and its effect on the spec audit recorded as a requirement-level risk? [Dependency, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK034 Does every functional requirement map to at least one user story and one success criterion, or is the gap stated? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK035 Is a requirement ID scheme established that tasks, contracts and the issue map reference consistently? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]

## Ambiguities and Open Decisions

- [ ] CHK036 Are the three open decisions (authoritative version source when instructions are silent, who stamps the changelog, one adapter module or two) tied to the requirements each one changes? [Ambiguity, Spec §Open Decisions]
- [ ] CHK037 Are the provisional answers recorded in research clearly distinguished from decided requirements in the spec? [Ambiguity, Spec §Open Decisions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Candidate findings noticed while writing this checklist, for the reviewer to confirm: CHK015 (priority conflict between US2 and US3), CHK032 (engine location versus portability) and CHK011 (length rule not stated in the spec)
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
